thought.text: In upstream `master`, `settings` is loaded **first**; in this pinned commit, `projekts` is loaded first — so the map settings don't exist yet when the first Projekt creates its MapLocation. Let me confirm a14's settings seed to see how this ever worked:

reasoning_content:
In upstream master, `settings` is loaded **first**, before everything else. In this repo (the pinned commit), `projekts` is first, then `settings`. This is a known bug in this version of the seed file — it was later fixed in master by loading settings first.

Wait, let me double-check: in this repo's `db:dev_seed`, the order is:
1. projekts (creates Projekt → needs map settings)
2. settings (creates the settings including map settings)

So the projekts seed runs before the map settings exist. That's why it fails.

But wait — is this really a bug in the repo, or is the seed supposed to work some other way? Let me think about it. In the a14 release, the order is also projekts first, then settings. Let me check whether upstream a14 also has this issue... no, actually, the seed must work in upstream a14. Let me check the a14 version of `settings.rb` — maybe map settings were seeded in a different way, or maybe projekts.rb was different.

No wait — let me reconsider. The a14 I downloaded has the same projekts.rb. Let me check the a14 settings.rb and see whether `map.*` was included there.

Actually, the issue might be more subtle. Let me look again at `Projekt.create!(name: 'Test1')`. This triggers `copy_map_settings` → `MapLocation.default` → `MapLocation.find_or_create_by!(default: true)` → `new_record?` is true → `set_default_values` → mappable is nil → goes into the `else` branch → `self.latitude ||= default ? Setting["map.latitude"] : ...`.

The record being created is the default MapLocation (default: true), so `default` is true → `Setting["map.latitude"]` is used. At that point, map settings don't exist (they get seeded later). Therefore `Setting["map.latitude"]` returns nil → latitude is nil → validation fails.

In other words, in a14, the seed really does have an ordering bug, but... no wait, maybe in a14 the settings seed was different. Let me check a14's settings.rb.
